name: Manda Airport
before:
The airport for Lamu, on Manda Island off the Kenyan coast, about 450 km by air south east of Nairobi.

The transfer is the thing to build into an itinerary. The airport is not on Lamu Island itself, so arriving clients take a short boat ride across to Lamu Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, or on to Shela.

It is a small operation with basic facilities, handling domestic flights from Nairobi, Mombasa and Malindi. There is a paved runway of 6,330 feet and a shorter unpaved strip, at an elevation of just 6 metres.

The airport is also known as Lamu Airport, so both names turn up in supplier systems.
after:
The airport for Lamu, on Manda Island off the Kenyan coast. It is also known as Lamu Airport, so both names turn up in supplier systems.

The transfer is the thing to build into an itinerary. Clients land on Manda Island, not on Lamu Island itself, so the onward journey is by boat. Lamu Old Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is on Lamu Island.

Domestic flights come in from Nairobi, Mombasa and Malindi.

The FCDO advises against all travel to Lamu County except Lamu Island and Manda Island, and says visitors to the islands should fly into Lamu airport rather than travel by road.

claims.note: Was 'a short boat ride across to Lamu Town ... or on to Shela'. Wikipedia gives the boat to Lamu Island; the second source is a resort on Manda Island itself (The Majlis, live FAQ), which meets guests at Manda Airport by speedboat. That is a hotel page, the lowest tier; the airline and tourist-board pages that would say the same (Safarilink, Airkenya, Kenya Airways, Magical Kenya) sit behind bot checks. 'Short' and the Shela leg are dropped.

claims.claim: about 450 km by air south east of Nairobi
claims.wasBefore: about 450 km by air south east of Nairobi
claims.why: Wikipedia alone (it cites an online distance calculator). The coordinates check measures from Lamu, not Nairobi, and no second written source gives the distance or bearing.

claims.claim: short boat ride to Lamu Town or on to Shela
claims.wasBefore: so arriving clients take a short boat ride across to Lamu Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, or on to Shela
claims.why: Reworded. The boat is kept, with the resort's airport speedboat as the second source. No source says clients go from the airport on to Shela (Jambojet says only that Shela Beach is a short boat ride from Lamu Town, and Wikipedia calls Shela an island), so Shela goes. The UNESCO site is named as Lamu Old Town.

claims.wasBefore: It is a small operation with basic facilities
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The Kenya Airports Authority's page for the airport (kaa.go.ke) answers with a Cloudflare challenge.

claims.claim: paved runway of 6,330 feet and a shorter unpaved strip
claims.wasBefore: There is a paved runway of 6,330 feet and a shorter unpaved strip
claims.why: Not settled, as the drafting note asked. Wikipedia contradicts itself (a single runway in its lead, two runways in its body), and it and OurAirports disagree on the paved runway (1,930 m or 6,330 ft against 2,000 m or 6,561 ft), though they agree on an unpaved 931 m strip. The Kenya Airports Authority site is behind a Cloudflare challenge and Kenya's eAIP (eaip.kcaa.or.ke) needs a login, so neither official source could be read.

claims.wasBefore: at an elevation of just 6 metres
claims.why: OurAirports gives the same 6 m (20 ft) as Wikipedia, so it is confirmed, but it went with the runway sentence it belonged to and is of no use for booking.
